correction.text: the Franconian principality of Ansbach, a stand-in circle

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Ansbach row). The page gives no area ('Area and population: not given') and none of its districts (Neustadt an der Aisch, Schwabach, Uffenheim, Gunzenhausen, Cadolzburg and Roth are not mentioned); a 28 km circle at Ansbach (about 2,460 km2), soft. The personal union with Bayreuth (1769-1791) and with Brandenburg (1415-1440) do not change it.

ledger.note: 21 January 1398: the principality. 'The principality was established following the death of Frederick V, Burgrave of Nuremberg, on 21 January 1398'; his lands were split between his sons Frederick VI (Ansbach) and John III (Bayreuth).

region.text: the lands of the Ansbach line round Ansbach

ledger.note: 21 September 1440: Ansbach to Albert. Frederick VI 'had become Elector Frederick I of Brandenburg in 1415' (personal union with Brandenburg 1415-1440); 'On 21 September 1440, almost three years after Frederick's death his territories were divided between his sons', Ansbach going to Albert. Same state, new line.

2 December 1791: the sale to Prussia. Charles Alexander 'sold the sovereignty of his principalities to King Frederick William II of Prussia'; 'Ansbach was formally annexed on 28 January 1792'. Charles Alexander had held Bayreuth too since 1769.

certainty.note: The page gives no boundary or area; the circle is a stand-in.

SHAPE. A 28 km circle at Ansbach (10.57E 49.30N). Gazetteer names wanted: 'Ansbach'.

NOT SETTLED. (1) Area, boundary and acquisitions (the Kulmbach inheritance of 1603 and the Sayn-Altenkirchen inheritance of 1741 are not on the page). (2) 1603: the page mentions no partition; Joachim Ernst's accession is the only 1603 item. (3) The personal union with Bayreuth (1769-1791) is not territory. (4) End: the sale is 2 December 1791, the formal annexation 28 January 1792. (5) 1806 (Bavaria) is not on the page.
